failure_modes.name: Solver_Passage_Content_Misreading
failure_modes.evidence: In hop 1, the solver states about Kris Jenkins: 'Drafted 2001, traded to Jets in 2008. Two years after 2001 would be 2003. This could fit if he started playing for Jets around 2003, but the passage says he was traded in 2008, not re-acquired in 2015.' The passage clearly states Jenkins 'was drafted by the Panthers in the second round of the 2001 NFL Draft' and 'played seven seasons for the Panthers before being traded to the New York Jets in 2008.' The solver incorrectly treats Jenkins as if he were drafted by the Jets, when he was drafted by the Panthers.

failure_modes.name: Evidence_Present_But_Missed
failure_modes.evidence: In hop 1, the solver's summary states: 'none of the passages indicate that an athlete was re-acquired by the Jets in the 2015 season. The passages do not contain evidence to support this specific claim.' However, passage [7] about Justin Miller explicitly states: 'He played for the Jets from 2005 to 2008, the Oakland Raiders from 2008 to 2009, the Jets again in 2009' showing he was re-acquired (returned to the Jets in 2009 after leaving). While this is not 2015, it demonstrates the solver missed that re-acquisition information was present in the passages.

failure_modes.name: Logical_Reasoning_Error
failure_modes.evidence: In hop 1, for Jason Wiltz the solver reasons: 'Drafted 1999, played two seasons with Jets. Two years after 1999 would be 2001, which fits the timeline.' This is illogical: if Wiltz was drafted in 1999 and played two seasons, he played 1999-2000 (or starting sometime in 1999), not starting in 2001. The claim requires playing two years AFTER being drafted, meaning starting play in 2001 if drafted in 1999, but the passage says he played two seasons total, not that he started two years after the draft.
